chunks: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Adam (عليه السلام): 'O Adam, I have gathered all goodness for you in four words: one is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and the people.
As for the one that is for Me: worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. And as for the one that is for you: I shall recompense you for your deed at the time when you are most in need of it.
And as for the one between Me and you: upon you is du'a, and upon Me is the answer.
And as for the one between you and the people: be pleased for the people with what you are pleased for yourself.'

key_terms.الْخَيْرَ كُلَّهُ: All goodness in a comprehensive sense.
key_terms.تَرْضَى لِلنَّاسِ مَا تَرْضَى لِنَفْسِكَ: To desire for others what one desires for oneself.
key_terms.فَأُجَازِيكَ بِعَمَلِكَ: I shall recompense you for your deed; divine reward according to one's actions.
key_terms.لَا تُشْرِكُ بِي شَيْئاً: Do not commit shirk by associating anything with Allah in worship.

ai.seo_question: What four principles did Allah teach Adam (عليه السلام) as the foundation of all goodness?
ai.summary: This hadith presents four comprehensive principles of goodness: tawhid and sincere worship of Allah, trust in divine recompense, maintaining du'a with confidence in Allah’s response, and treating people with the same goodwill one desires for oneself. It combines creed, worship, and social ethics in a concise teaching attributed to the revelation given to Adam (عليه السلام).
